metadata.title: Amazon India e-commerce exports hit $27bn, eyes $80bn by 2030

content.text:
E-commerce giant Amazon has reached $27bn in cumulative e-commerce exports from India through the Amazon Global Selling program, progressing towards an $80bn target by 2030.
Cumulative shipments grew by $7bn this year, matching the previous year's increase when total exports rose from $13bn at the end of 2024 to $20bn in October 2025.
Introduced in 2015, the programme has registered upwards of 240,000 Indian exporters who have together sold more than one billion items across international marketplaces operated by Amazon.
The merchant base grew by 20% over the past year, covering 28 states, seven union territories, and upwards of 200 cities and towns.
During 2026, leading export destinations comprised the US, the UK, Germany, Canada, the UAE, France, Italy, and Spain.
Amazon Global Selling India head Srinidhi Kalvapudi said: "India has the potential to become a global powerhouse for consumer exports, and ecommerce is helping turn that ambition into reality, creating opportunities for every Indian seller to become a global exporter.
"As we work towards our $80bn exports commitment by 2030, our focus is on making global selling simpler and more accessible through AI-led innovation, capacity building and stronger ecosystem partnerships, while supporting the Government of India's vision to take Brand India to the world."
Health and personal care was the fastest-growing merchandise category, delivering a 45% compound annual growth rate across the previous decade.
This was followed by grocery at 44%, beauty at 42%, toys at 35%, home goods at 30%, furniture at 27%, and apparel at 23%.
Across regions, the National Capital Territory of Delhi recorded the highest number of exporters with over 36,000 sellers, followed by Rajasthan (32,500+), Uttar Pradesh (29,000+), Gujarat (28,000+), and Maharashtra (23,500+).
To facilitate sector-focused commerce, 'Amazon Global Selling' signed memoranda of understanding with the Apparel Export Promotion Council, the Carpet Export Promotion Council, and The Cotton Textiles Export Promotion Council, alongside an onboarding drive in Bhadohi, Uttar Pradesh for rug manufacturers.
These accords and ongoing consultations with the Ministry of Textiles correspond with the Government of India's target of $100bn in textile exports by 2030, supported by 2026 category growth of 30% in home products and 23% in apparel.
The rise in cumulative exports follows Amazon's announcement in June of an additional $13bn for Indian cloud and AI infrastructure, supplementing a $35bn investment announced in 2025.
"Amazon India e-commerce exports hit $27bn, eyes $80bn by 2030" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.
